_note: Story 29.1-001 recorded evidence — real `qwen -p --yolo` run via scripts/qwen-worktree-smoke.sh against a scratch repo with 2 concurrent git worktrees. Not a scoreboard: qwen never got past its own auth check in either worktree, so the worktree-isolation question the story asks is verified-negative on this host, not silently abandoned.

root_cause: No qwen auth type is configured on this host, and the CLI's own `qwen auth` subcommand is marked '(removed)' in v0.21.10 — there is no headless way to configure one either. A prior probe (controller/eval/results/qwen-preflight-failure.json, story 31.3-001) also tried `--auth-type qwen-oauth`, which reports the free OAuth tier was discontinued on 2026-04-15; a paid provider credential (Coding Plan, OpenRouter, Fireworks AI, ...) would be needed to get past this check.
approval_flag_found: --yolo (equivalently --approval-mode yolo) is accepted by qwen 0.21.10 for unattended tool execution, even though it is undocumented in `qwen --help`. It was exercised in this run; it did not by itself unblock the auth check.
conclusion: The worktree-isolation question (does an edit stay confined to its own worktree, and do concurrent worktrees stay isolated from each other and the repo root) was answered PASS as a side effect — both worktrees, both failing identically, left zero cross-contamination and the scratch repo root stayed clean. But qwen never completed the requested edit task in either worktree, so AC1's 'the task completes' condition is not met. Per AC5, `worktree_isolation` and `parallel` stay `false` in harnesses.yaml pending a host with configured qwen auth; this story closes as verified-negative.
